name: Escape from Dead Orchard
description: Leaving Dead Orchard from bottom releases the high both-arm leg triangle and restores guard frames. The top player is the one defending the captured arms.
summary: Leaving Dead Orchard from the bottom releases the high both-arm leg triangle and returns the knees and frames to a comfortable guard.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Dead Orchard Control, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The bottom player owns the arm trap. The opponent who must escape the trap is the top player, so releasing the guard and escaping its attack are different actions.

The bottom player faces the opponent and keeps the hips close beneath the shoulders. The legs form a high figure-four around the shoulder line, with both opposing arms inside. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Nathan Orchard — Dead Orchard, part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XoiB1D2WJwE); [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo).

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): Which enclosure do your legs open for this reset?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player releases their own both-arm high leg triangle before restoring a more comfortable guard.
flashcards.answer_line: The high triangle around both arms

plausible: A high triangle enclosing only one arm
Your ankles crossed low around the waist
trap: A high shin grip with no figure-four closed

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): What hand action precedes releasing the leg triangle?
flashcards.answer: Remove wrist leverage and any elbow loading before freeing the arms from the legs.
flashcards.answer_line: Let go of any wrist leverage on the captured elbow

plausible: Pull the wrist as the legs separate
Keep the arm extended until both legs lower
trap: Release the shin grip while keeping the wrist lever

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): What moves to lower the high leg without knee torque?
flashcards.answer: Use a comfortable hip angle to lower the released leg; avoid pulling the foot against a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip movement with the knee supported

plausible: The foot turns while the thigh stays fixed
The ankle is pulled while the knee stays wedged
trap: The torso turns while the high figure-four stays shut

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): Where must the returning knee fit to retain guard?
flashcards.answer: Bring the knee into the space protected by the inside forearm rather than letting the passer fill that gap.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside between your torso and the opponent

plausible: Outside the passer's near hip beside your elbow
Behind the passer while your torso turns away
trap: Against the far hip with the near torso gap open

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): How should your torso orient as the legs lower?
flashcards.answer: Maintain a facing relationship while the released high legs return to guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep the shoulders and hips facing the opponent

plausible: Turn the shoulders away and leave the hips behind
Turn the hips away while reaching toward the opponent
trap: Face away before the inside knee has returned

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): What must recover before you reach for another submission?
flashcards.answer: Stabilize posture, knee comfort and inside space before beginning another attack.
flashcards.answer_line: A comfortable knee position and inside guard space

plausible: A new wrist grip while both knees stay bypassed
High feet with the knees still spread outside
trap: A shoulder frame while the hips remain folded

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): Where should the upper forearm block an approaching crossface?
flashcards.answer: An inside shoulder frame limits crossface and chest pressure while a knee returns.

plausible: Outside the opponent's far elbow
At the near wrist with your elbow flared
trap: Against the hip with the shoulder path unframed

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (bottom): What makes this action a guard reset rather than a trap escape?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player owns the arm trap; the top player is the one whose arms must escape it.
flashcards.answer_line: You are releasing the legs that held their arms

plausible: You are drawing your arms out of their high legs
You are lifting above their knee hug from top
trap: You are pulling their wrists through your closed legs

defender.name: Escape from Dead Orchard Defender
defender.description: Escape from Dead Orchard (defender): Treat a high leg triangle containing both your arms as an arm-lock threat even when the neck is not being choked. Keep the arms compact and avoid offering a straight arm while trying to force posture.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Dead Orchard Control, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The bottom player owns the arm trap. The opponent who must escape the trap is the top player, so releasing the guard and escaping its attack are different actions.

Treat a high leg triangle containing both your arms as an arm-lock threat even when the neck is not being choked. Keep the arms compact and avoid offering a straight arm while trying to force posture. Maintain an early frame at the hip or thigh before the figure-four closes around the shoulders.

Work on opening the leg enclosure before withdrawing the shoulder and elbow together; stop if an arm is already loaded. Only raise posture after the shoulder line is free; a sudden pull can extend a captured elbow. Use a verbal tap or foot tap if both hands are trapped, and do not rely on pain to judge remaining range.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
key_principles: Recognize both-arm capture: Treat a high leg triangle containing both your arms as an arm-lock threat even when the neck is not being choked.
Protect the elbows: Keep the arms compact and avoid offering a straight arm while trying to force posture.
Prevent the leg closure: Maintain an early frame at the hip or thigh before the figure-four closes around the shoulders.
Clear a shoulder safely: Work on opening the leg enclosure before withdrawing the shoulder and elbow together; stop if an arm is already loaded.
Recover base in stages: Only raise posture after the shoulder line is free; a sudden pull can extend a captured elbow.
Tap with any free signal: Use a verbal tap or foot tap if both hands are trapped, and do not rely on pain to judge remaining range.

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (top): What can happen if one trapped arm straightens?
flashcards.answer: The both-arm triangle can support short arm isolation when a captured elbow straightens.
flashcards.answer_line: A short elbow-extension lock from below

plausible: The elbow slips free because straightening enlarges the triangle
The shoulder clears before the elbow reaches extension
trap: The high legs drop to the hips as the wrist withdraws

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (top): What arm posture should you preserve while seeking release?
flashcards.answer: Keep the arms compact while addressing the actual leg enclosure rather than forcing posture through extended arms.
flashcards.answer_line: Compact elbows instead of long reaching posts

plausible: Both arms extended through the high legs
One wrist drawn back while its shoulder stays fixed
trap: Elbows flared outside while the wrists remain held

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (top): When can a hip frame help prevent the triangle?
flashcards.answer: Use hip or thigh framing early; once the triangle and arm lock are secured, obtain release rather than relying on the same frame.
flashcards.answer_line: Before the high legs close around the shoulders

plausible: After the high figure-four has fixed both shoulders
After wrist leverage has loaded a captured elbow
trap: Whenever the chin lifts despite retained shoulders

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (top): What should follow an opening around one shoulder?
flashcards.answer: Use the opening to recover shoulder and elbow as a unit; stop if another retained connection prevents free movement.
flashcards.answer_line: Withdraw that shoulder and elbow together

plausible: Pull only the wrist while the upper arm stays caught
Lift the chest while leaving the elbow behind
trap: Turn the torso first while the elbow stays in the legs

flashcards.question: Escape from Dead Orchard (top): What confirms that upright posture is available?
flashcards.answer: Raise the chest only after clearing the shoulder line, with no trapped arm being pulled into extension.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulders clear of the high legs

plausible: Only your nose points above the shin
Only your free hand touches the mat
trap: The opponent relaxes one wrist grip
